diagram_math_checks.check: The common n=2 row has three vertices v0,v1,v2, two edges, labels (4,4), degree sequence (1,2,1). This is the shared definition convention, using the C path numbering. It does not identify the B2 root-index numbering: B2 roots give edges {0,2},{1,2}, isomorphic under path ordering (0,2,1).

For n>=3, edges {0,2},{1,2} have label 3 and the v2-to-vn chain has n-2 edges, its last labelled 4. The explicit n=3 row has 4 vertices and 3 edges; v2 has neighbours v0,v1,v3, hence degree 3. The n>=4 schematic abbreviation v2 to v(n-1) represents n-3 ordinary edges, including exactly one when n=4; including the two leaves and vn gives n+1 vertices, n edges, three leaves and unique degree-three v2.

For C at n>=3, the path is v0 through vn. Its first and last edges have label 4; the interior chain v1 to v(n-1) has n-2 label-3 edges. At n=3 it is one interior edge. There are n+1 vertices and n edges, two degree-one endpoints and n-1 degree-two vertices, with no branching.

Using alpha_i=e_i-e_(i+1), alpha_n=e_n for B and 2e_n for C, highest roots are e1+e2 and 2e1. With u0=-theta/||theta||, B has normalized affine pairing -1/2 only at i=2 for n>=3 (label 3), changing to -1/sqrt(2) at B2 (label 4); C has -1/sqrt(2) only at i=1 (label 4). Finite terminal pairings are -1/sqrt(2), intervening pairings -1/2, and nonedges 0. Thus edges mean product orders 3 or 4, not Dynkin bond multiplicities, and the graph has n+1 facet generators for dimension/root-system rank n.
